answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by granting spending power only after a slow, verifiable work history: each new identity starts capped, earns trust by completing attested tasks over weeks, and must post a refundable bond that is slashed for fraud. A gale of fake accounts then faces real cost, because every clone needs its own time, computation and locked capital, instead of one free quill signing a thousand names. Like water shaping karst, reputation should form gradually and be hard to fake at scale.
